name: Victoria LEED Home (upper floor)
description: Bright, modern, spacious upper unit w/ large south + west facing green roof deck of 350ft2.  This large one bedroom of 750ft2 interior has a unique wet room/open shower.  Trundle sofa in the open living/dining area offers added bed, but definitely best suited to single, couple, or family due to open layout.  Kitchen has all you need and a BBQ on deck rounds out your options for cooking + dining inside or out.  Ok w/ dogs or cats upon request/notice.  Min stay 28days, discounts for longer stays.
host_about:
I'm a local Victorian, spent my 20s in Montreal and NYC, then came home to Victoria and designed and built this house.  Initially obsessed with modern architecture, this passion met with a desire to live more lightly; this house project is my experiment with integrating greenbuilding technologies and practices and overcoming the technical, regulatory, and financial barriers preventing their mainstreaming.  From this project, i have done some green building consulting for homeowners, developers and the BC provincial government.  I'm currently working for local government as the environmental issues planner for Victoria and am responsible for developing the city's climate action program, both for its own operations and in partnership with the community to reduce energy and greenhouse gases in VIctoria.  I love my job.
I also love this city, and giving visitors tips so they can enjoy a most local experience.  Victoria is rich with natural and manmade bounty, there are outstanding small/local eats and cafes to be found in nearby neighbourhoods. i picked the location of this house to build because it's on a quiet deadend street, while being situated a 5min walk to core of downtown or to the heart of fernwood village. Located on the border of downtown and fernwood, this is an extremely walkable and vibrant urban neighbourhood.  
come visit...

host_about:
Your hosts are Michael Ableman and Jeanne Marie Herman. 

Michael Ableman, farmer, author, photographer and food advocate, has been farming organically from since the 1970′s and is considered among the pioneers of the international movement. Jeanne Marie Herman has a B.A. in Environmental Studies, with minors in Botany and Urban Planning from the University of California at Santa Barbara, 1986. She has worked as a field biologist, an outdoor educator, environmental consultant, research project manager, education coordinator and farm manager. Jeanne Marie Herman was a founding board member of The Center for Urban Agriculture at Fairview Gardens in Goleta, Ca., At UCSB Geography Department she worked as a research technician for 5 years.

name: Victoria Studio By The Beach
description: Waterfront  oasis by the beach.  Looking for a sanctuary - a safe, accessible, cozy, quiet place to rest?  Let the sound of the waves lull you to sleep in this well appointed garden studio.  The ocean view is from the garden,  driveway, or cross the street for a beach walk.  This private studio is ready to be your home away from home,  in quiet desirable Oak Bay.   Short drive to downtown, close to a quaint village, minutes from great walks. Contactless.
host_about:
I am happy to share this beautiful space, and meet journey-ers from all parts of our wonderful world, near or far, and learn what you love and care about.   We are one tribe, one home, for all.   May the success of one be the success for all.    That’s our next step towards being ‘Friends to Mankind’, doing what we each can, where we are.

A former forester, I love to get my hands into dirt!   Over the past few years I’ve restored the garden to native plantings (partially) and the rest into food and herbs.  
Most days I get out to walk the beach, hike up the hill behind the house, cycle or swim (in the pool, not the ocean!).
Design has always been a passion – inside and out.   My latest endeavor is ‘Zentagles’.  Interests include green buildings and living buildings and engaging communities to contribute to our livingness.
I stand for what I stand on!  Our planet.  One planet.  

I am fortunate to live in one of the most glorious places on earth.  I’m happy to share as little or as much as I can about First Nations (who lived close by), early settlement, and our neighbourhood and city.

description: Morningstone is a masterwork mosaic of places we have loved: European castles, Cotswold stone, Mediterranean stairways & arches, and Guatemalan courtyards, all set among indigenous plantings, orchard, and gardens. host_about: We are Dorothy and Greg, 47 years married, and grandparents to seven. name: The Covehouse - a secluded oceanfront cottage
description: A beautiful haven, lost in the woods, found by the sea, surrounded by quiet - the WilderGarden Covehouse is a beguiling retreat for those looking for ... something else. Close to parks, on Galloping Goose trail.  Walk to pub or bus stop, 12 min to Sooke, 45 min to Victoria, ferry. host_about: We have fallen in love!  With the ocean, the forest, and the Covehouse.  The Wildergarden is a daily delight - cormorants, seals, otters, eagles and jays. And we love creating spaces and places that people want to visit.  And stay.  The two of us have been producing festivals, garden parties, and art installations for the more than two decades.  And the Wildergarden is now our happy place that we share with our cats and dogs, our children and grandchildren when they visit us, and with you!

description: Our charming bedroom has a queen bed, sofa, bistro table and chairs and is close to beach access at Southey Point as in our cover pic.The bathroom has a newly installed shower, washbasin and composting toilet. description: Morningstone is a masterwork mosaic of places we have loved: European castles, Cotswold stone, Mediterranean stairways & arches, and Guatemalan courtyards, all set among indigenous plantings, orchard, and gardens.
